worked_solution:
Note that plugging in $x=3$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{{x}^{3}-27}{x-3} & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{[{x}^{3}-27]^{′}}{[x-3]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{3{x}^{2}}{1} \\  & =3(3)^{2} \\  & =27\end{aligned}
$$
